Homogeneous polynomials

Throughout, \mathbb K is \mathbb R or \mathbb C (an RCLike field) and X, Y are normed spaces over \mathbb K. A continuous n-homogeneous polynomial P\colon X\to Y is a map of the form P(x)=L(x,\ldots,x) for some continuous n-linear map L (IsHomPoly). Its norm is the supremum over the closed unit ball, \|P\| = \sup_{\|x\|\le 1}\|P(x)\| (polyNorm). This module collects the elementary facts about diagonals of multilinear maps and their symmetrizations used everywhere else.

noncomputable sectionopen scoped BigOperatorsopen Finsetnamespace LindenstraussPolynomialsvariable {𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜]variable {X : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace 𝕜 X]variable {Y : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup Y] [NormedSpace 𝕜 Y]

Continuous n-linear maps X × ⋯ × X → Y.

abbrev MLin (𝕜 : Type*) [RCLike 𝕜] (X : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace 𝕜 X] (Y : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup Y] [NormedSpace 𝕜 Y] (n : ℕ) := ContinuousMultilinearMap 𝕜 (fun _ : Fin n => X) Y

The diagonal x ↦ A (x, …, x) of a multilinear map: the associated polynomial.

def diag {n : ℕ} (A : MLin 𝕜 X Y n) (x : X) : Y := A (fun _ => x)

A multilinear map is symmetric if it is invariant under permutations of its arguments.

def IsSymm {n : ℕ} (A : MLin 𝕜 X Y n) : Prop := ∀ (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (v : Fin n → X), A (v ∘ σ) = A v

P : X → Y is a continuous n-homogeneous polynomial: P x = L (x, …, x) for some continuous n-linear map L.

def IsHomPoly (𝕜 : Type*) [RCLike 𝕜] {X : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace 𝕜 X] {Y : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup Y] [NormedSpace 𝕜 Y] (n : ℕ) (P : X → Y) : Prop := ∃ L : MLin 𝕜 X Y n, ∀ x, P x = L (fun _ => x)

The sup norm over the closed unit ball: ‖P‖ = sup_{‖x‖ ≤ 1} ‖P x‖.

def polyNorm {E F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] (P : E → F) : ℝ := sSup ((fun x => ‖P x‖) '' Metric.closedBall (0 : E) 1)
